_about: ¿Me lo puede repetir?: Don Chuy behind the counter of the tourist information office (one set-up). 10 pictures: the welcome, the free map, the map unfolded (where to?), the café tip, the way (fast talk, pointing out the door), the long way down to the sea, the left-or-right quiz, going over the way again, the brochures (anything else?), goodbye. The tricky-word twist (banqueta / kiosco), the police question and the slow repeat have no id of their own and keep the route picture.

items.prompt: Don Chuy, the volunteer at the tourist information office, stands behind the wooden counter about one third from the left, both arms opened wide in welcome, leaning forward eagerly. An eager, open smile with raised eyebrows ("¡Hola, hola! ¡Bienvenido a Puerto Colibrí!"). On the counter in front of the learner: a neat stack of folded town maps with blank covers and a cup of pens.

Change only his pose: he holds out one folded town map across the counter toward the learner with both hands, its cover only a simple drawing of palms and sea with no words; eyebrows raised, beaming ("¿Quiere un mapa? ¡Es gratis!").

Change only his pose: the town map now lies unfolded on the counter, turned toward the learner (simple colored blocks for streets and buildings, a green square for the zócalo, blue sea along its bottom edge, one small red star near the middle, no words or numbers); he taps the red star with one finger and looks up with raised eyebrows ("Bueno, ¿a dónde va?").

Change only his pose: he holds up a small brochure whose cover is only a drawing of a steaming clay coffee cup (no words), his eyes half closed in bliss, the other hand on his heart (recommending Café La Ceiba: "¡El mejor café del pueblo!"); the unfolded map still on the counter.

Change only his pose: talking fast, he points with his whole arm out through the open door toward the street, his other hand drawing a quick turn in the air above the unfolded map; eyebrows up, mouth open mid-word, full of energy (giving the way, much too fast).
items.note: 5 Nov catch-up: also the ways the s62 audit added in town (confirm_church, confirm_clinic, confirm_busstop, confirm_taqueria): out the door and a quick turn, as every way in town.

items.prompt: Change only his pose: he leans over the unfolded map and runs one finger in a long line from the red star down to the blue sea at its bottom edge, looking up at the learner with a cheerful nod (the beach and the pier: a longer walk, down to the sea).
items.note: 5 Nov catch-up: also confirm_tours (the s62 audit's tours booth on the malecón by the pier: down to the sea). Since that audit the beach and the pier are two minutes away: the picture shows the way down to the sea, not a long walk.

items.prompt: Change only his pose: he holds both hands up at shoulder height, index fingers pointing out to either side like a game-show host, a playful, teasing grin (a quick quiz: left or right out the door?).
Change only his pose: he slowly traces the way on the unfolded map with the capped end of a pen, leaning in close, a patient, encouraging look (going over the way again, step by step).

Change only his pose: he fans out three brochures toward the learner, their covers pictures only (a turquoise cenote, stone ruins above the sea, a white beach with a sea turtle), no words; eyebrows raised, eager ("¿Algo más?").

Change only his pose: he waves goodbye with one hand raised high, the other hand on his chest, a big warm smile; the counter is clear except for the stack of maps and the cup of pens (the learner has taken the map).
